'''Christopher Stephen Copeland''' (born March 17, 1984), nicknamed "'''the X-Factor'''",<ref>{{citation|last=Hip-Hop & Clout Media|title=Crazy NY Knicks Fan Addresses The Haters|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bBPfw1pbkO0|date=May 12, 2013|access-date=May 28, 2019}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|University of Colorado, Boulder]].

==Early life==
Copeland was born in [[Orange, New Jersey]] to mother, Terry, in 1984. With his father absent from his life from birth, Copeland always looked up to his older brother, Vincent Alphaquan, a basketball standout at Seton Hall Prep and Columbus High School in New York before he played at Jackson State. At age 4, he established a practice routine with Vincent as his coach, honing his game with various dribbling drills in a narrow alleyway next to their house. He continued with the regimen through childhood at Elmwood Park under Vincent's guidance. This all changed in May 1997 when Vincent slipped into a coma after a drunk driver struck him in a hit-and-run accident on Central Avenue in East Orange, just a few blocks away from the Copelands' house. He regained consciousness for a couple days, but six weeks after the accident, he unexpectedly died. Vincent, engaged to marry that June, was 22.<ref name=nj>{{cite web | last=Castillo | first=Jorge | url=http://www.nj.com/knicks/index.ssf/2013/01/chris_copeland_newark_native_a.html | title=Chris Copeland, Newark native and Knicks reserve, made several difficult moves to get to the NBA | work=NJ.com | date=January 15, 2013 | access-date=December 6, 2014}}</ref>

One weekend in August 1999, Copeland and his mother visited his aunt in [[Richmond, Virginia]] where she brought Copeland, then 15, to nearby [[Hermitage High School (Virginia)|Hermitage High School]]. He wandered into the gym where, by chance, the school's players were running pick-up games. He was already 6-foot-6, and he was immediately noticed. Upon their chance encounter with the coaches at Hermitage, Terry decided she and her son would leave New Jersey. She quit her job as a senior administrator for Unity Hospice in Newark, and by October 1999, her son was enrolled at Hermitage.<ref name="nj" /> As a senior in 2001–02, he averaged 15 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.7 blocks per game for the Panthers as he earned Most Valuable Player honors, as well as Virginia High School Colonial District Co-Player of the Year, Virginia All-State honorable mention, all-region, all-district and all-metro first-team selection. As both a junior and senior, he helped Hermitage win the Colonial District Championship.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url=http://www.cubuffs.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=129 | title=#15 Chris Copeland | work=CUBuffs.com | access-date=September 17, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], Copeland proved to be a valuable contributor off the bench as he often provided CU with clutch points despite limited minutes. In 26 games, he averaged 2.5 points and 1.6 rebounds in 7.7 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/chris-copeland-1.html | title=Chris Copeland Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | access-date=December 6, 2014}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, Copeland played in 27 of the Buffs 28 games while averaging 9.2 minutes per game. He scored a season-high 12 points against Iowa State on March 3, 2004, along with five rebounds and four-of-four from the free-throw line. For the season, he averaged 2.9 points and 2.5 rebounds per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, Copeland earned Big 12 All-Improved team honors after more than tripling his points per game average. He scored a career-high 25 points against Richmond on January 4, 2005. In 29 games (15 starts), he averaged 11.7 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 blocks in 25.2 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, Copeland helped CU to a 20–10 overall record and an NIT berth as he played in all 30 games with 28 starts while averaging 24.3 minutes per game. He scored a season-high 22 points against Kansas on January 11, 2006. For the season, he averaged 12.1 points, 5.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.1 blocks per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==
===Fort Worth Flyers (2006–2007)===
Copeland went undrafted in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. On March 29, 2007, he was acquired by the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |title=NBA Development League: 2006–07 D-League Transactions Index |work=NBA.com |access-date=April 8, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618011602/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |archive-date=June 18, 2015 |df=mdy }}</ref> He went on to play 20 games for the Flyers to close out the 2006–07 season.

===CB L'Hospitalet (2007)===
On September 20, 2007, Copeland signed with [[CB L'Hospitalet]] of Spain for the 2007–08 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.feb.es/NoticiaDesarrollo.aspx?idNoticia=15427|title=L'Hospitalet incorpora al pívot Chris Copeland|work=FEB.es|date=September 20, 2007|access-date=July 29, 2015|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Matrixx Magixx (2007–2008)===
In October 2007, Copeland left L'Hospitalet and signed with [[Matrixx Magixx]] of the Netherlands for the rest of the 2007–08 season.

===TBB Trier (2008–2010)===
In the summer of 2008, Copeland signed with [[TBB Trier]] of Germany for the 2008–09 season. In June 2009, he re-signed with the Trier for the 2009–10 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/77476/chris-copeland-stays-with-tbb-trier.html|title=Chris Copeland stays with TBB Trier|date=June 21, 2009|work=Sportando|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> He played 67 games over two seasons as he averaged 13.2 ppg in 2008–09 and 16.9 ppg in 2009–10.

===Okapi Aalstar (2010–2012)===
In July 2010, Copeland signed with [[Okapi Aalstar]] of Belgium for the 2010–11 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/belgium/83704/okapi-aalstar-signs-chris-copeland.html|title=Okapi Aalstar signs Chris Copeland|date=July 29, 2010|work=Sportando|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> In April 2011, he signed a two-year contract extension with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/belgium/86015/okapi-aalstar-extends-with-chris-copeland.html|title=Okapi Aalstar extends with Chris Copeland|date=April 16, 2011|work=Sportando|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> However, he left Aalstar following the 2011–12 season after earning [[Basketball League Belgium Division I MVP|Belgian League MVP]] and [[Basketball League Belgium Division I Star of the Coaches|Star of the Coaches]] honors.

===New York Knicks (2012–2013)===
On July 16, 2012, Copeland signed a one-year deal with the [[New York Knicks]] and went on to average 13.8 points in five games for the Knicks during the 2012 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10532|title=Knicks sign forward Chris Copeland|work=InsideHoops.com|date=July 16, 2012|access-date=April 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023062049/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10532|archive-date=October 23, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 2, 2012, he made his NBA debut in the Knicks' season opener against the [[Miami Heat]], recording no points in just under two minutes of action.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121102/MIANYK/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Knicks 104, Heat 84|work=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2012|access-date=April 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130122095147/http://www.nba.com/games/20121102/MIANYK/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 22, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 18, 2012, Copeland was assigned to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/new_york_knicks_assign_chris_c_2012_12_18.html |title=NBA Development League: New York Knicks Assign Chris Copeland and James White to NBA D-League Affiliate Erie BayHawks |work=NBA.com |date=December 18, 2012 |access-date=April 8, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320090343/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/new_york_knicks_assign_chris_c_2012_12_18.html |archive-date=March 20, 2015 }}</ref> He was recalled on December 19, reassigned on December 20 and recalled again on December 21; he did not appear in a game for Erie during his time with them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/knicks_recall_three_from_bayha_2012_12_21.html |title=NBA Development League: Knicks Recall Three from BayHawks |work=NBA.com |date=December 21, 2012 |access-date=April 8, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210180106/http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/knicks_recall_three_from_bayha_2012_12_21.html |archive-date=February 10, 2015 }}</ref>

On April 17, 2013, Copeland recorded a career-high 33 points in the Knicks' final regular season game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130417/ATLNYK/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Knicks 98, Hawks 92|work=NBA.com|date=April 17, 2015|access-date=April 17, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028054725/http://www.nba.com/games/20130417/ATLNYK/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 28, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He subsequently won the Eastern Conference [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award|Rookie of the Month]] for the month of April.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/19/copeland-lillard-kia-rookie-of-the-month/|title=Copeland, Lillard named Rookies of the Month|date=April 20, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> In 2012–13, Copeland averaged 8.7 points per game, and despite not being named to an [[NBA All-Rookie Team]], he still managed to tie [[Harrison Barnes]] at sixth place in the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]] voting (with eight points each).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/kia-rookie-of-the-year-lillard/|title=Portland's Lillard named 2012–13 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year|date=May 1, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180118231137/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/kia-rookie-of-the-year-lillard/|archive-date=January 18, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On June 25, 2013, the Knicks extended a qualifying offer to make Copeland a restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/228367/Knicks-Extend-Qualifying-Offer-To-Chris-Copeland|title=Knicks Extend Qualifying Offer To Chris Copeland|work=RealGM.com|date=June 25, 2013|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2013–2015)===
[[File:Chris Copeland (15537489920).jpg|thumb|Copeland with the Pacers in November 2014]]
On July 10, 2013, Copeland received a two-year, $6.1 million offer sheet from the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/nba--chris-copeland-agrees-to-deal-with-pacers-001801963.html|title=Chris Copeland agrees to deal with Pacers|date=July 6, 2013|work=Sports.Yahoo.com|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> The Knicks declined to match the offer, and Copeland signed with the Pacers on July 14.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-free-agent-chris-copeland|title=Pacers Sign Free Agent Chris Copeland|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 14, 2013|access-date=July 14, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/14/pacers-copeland-signed.ap/|title=Pacers announce official signing of Copeland|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 14, 2013|access-date=July 14, 2013}}</ref> After a promising rookie season with the Knicks, Copeland's production dropped off dramatically with the Pacers in 2013–14 as he averaged just 3.7 points and 6.5 minutes in 41 games, playing behind [[Paul George]], [[Danny Granger]] and [[Evan Turner]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/copelch01/gamelog/2014/|title=Chris Copeland 2013–14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref>

On November 5, 2014, Copeland recorded 19 points and a career-high 12 rebounds in a 94–96 overtime loss to the Washington Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141105/INDWAS/gameinfo.html|title=Wizards win 4th in row, top Pacers 96–94 in OT|work=NBA.com|date=November 6, 2014|access-date=April 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312195255/http://www.nba.com/games/20141105/INDWAS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 12, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2015–2016)===
On July 29, 2015, Copeland signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-chris-copeland|title=BUCKS SIGN CHRIS COPELAND|work=NBA.com|date=July 29, 2015|access-date=July 29, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Bucks in the team's season opener against the New York Knicks on October 28, recording 8 points and 2 rebounds in a 122–97 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Williams scores 24, Knicks beat Bucks 122–97 in opener|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026223709/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 26, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 22, 2016, he was waived by the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-steve-novak|title=BUCKS SIGN STEVE NOVAK|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2016|access-date=February 22, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, the [[Orlando Magic]] put in a waiver claim on Copeland in order to waive him, so as to go above the season's minimum team salary of $63 million.<ref>{{cite web|last=Robbins|first=Josh|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/magic-basketblog/os-magic-claim-chris-copeland-to-waive-him-20160224-story.html|title=Magic claim Chris Copeland to waive him|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=February 24, 2016|access-date=February 24, 2016}}</ref>

On September 22, 2016, Copeland signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-chris-copeland-and-robert-sacre|title=Pelicans Sign Chris Copeland and Robert Sacre|work=NBA.com|date=September 22, 2016|access-date=September 22, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 3.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pelicans Waive Chris Copeland|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-chris-copeland-10-3-16|access-date=October 3, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=October 3, 2016}}</ref>

After being waived by the Pelicans before playing a game for them, Copeland would never play in the NBA again and completed his professional basketball career overseas. His final NBA game was played on February 2, 2016, in a 95 - 107 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] where he played for nearly 3 minutes and only recorded 1 foul as a stat.

===Tofaş (2016–2017)===
On December 5, 2016, Copeland signed with Turkish club [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 Turkish Basketball Super League|2016–17 BSL season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CHRIS COPELAND TOFAŞ'TA|url=http://www.tofasspor.com/haber-715-chris_copeland_tofasta|access-date=December 5, 2016|work=tofasspor.com|date=December 5, 2016|language=Turkish}}</ref> He averaged 9 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game in 21 games of the 2016–17 BSL season, helping his club reach the playoffs.

===Andorra (2017–2018)===
On November 3, 2017, Copeland signed with [[BC Andorra|Andorra]]. He joined the club with an agreement until February 2018, in order to replace injured Georgian forward [[Beka Burjanadze]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Andorra officially signed Chris Copeland|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/546478/andorra-officially-signed-chris-copeland/|access-date=November 3, 2017|work=Eurohoops.net|date=November 3, 2017}}</ref> On January 29, 2018, he parted ways with Andorra after appearing in six games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Chris Copeland, MoraBanc Andorra part ways|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/spain/acb/262999/chris-copeland-morabanc-andorra-part-ways.html|access-date=January 29, 2018|work=Sportando.com|date=January 29, 2018}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On October 5, 2023, Copeland was hired as an assistant coach by the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wisconsin Herd Announce Assistant Coaching Staff for the 2023-24 Season|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announce-assistant-coaching-staff-for-the-2023-24-season/n-6020225|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 5, 2023|access-date=October 6, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On April 8, 2015, Copeland was stabbed in the abdomen outside of a nightclub in New York City. His ex-girlfriend, Katrine,<ref>{{cite web|last=Buckner|first=Candace|url=https://twitter.com/CandaceDBuckner/status/585800024661032960|title=I do know that Copeland and Katrine Saltara are...|work=Twitter.com|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> was also slashed in her arm and leg.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Colleen|last1=Long|first2=Verene|last2=Dobnik|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/08/indiana-pacers-chris-copeland-stabbed-at-new-york-city-night-club.ap/|title=Copeland in stable condition, apologizes for club incident|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> [[Pero Antić]] and [[Thabo Sefolosha]] of the [[Atlanta Hawks]] were arrested at the scene for allegedly interfering with police; the charges against Antic were later dropped, while Sefolosha refused a plea deal in favor of going to trial and was found not guilty, later suing the police for damages, including a broken tibia which had benched him for the remainder of that NBA season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13843715/atlanta-hawks-thabo-sefolosha-found-not-guilty-nyc-arrest-case|title=Hawks' Thabo Sefolosha found not guilty in NYC arrest case|work=ESPN.com|date=October 9, 2015|access-date=May 28, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19087188/thabo-sefolosha-atlanta-hawks-settles-lawsuit-vs-new-york-police-department-officers|title= Thabo Sefolosha settles lawsuit vs. 5 NYPD officers for $4 million |work=ESPN.com|date=April 5, 2017|access-date=May 28, 2026}}</ref> Copeland was taken to [[Bellevue Hospital]], where he was listed in stable condition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/indiana-pacers-chris-copeland-stabbed-nyc-club-article-1.2177265|title=Indiana Pacers forward Chris Copeland stabbed at 1 OAK club; two Atlanta Hawks arrested in aftermath: NYPD sources|first1=Kerry|last1=Burke|first2=Caitlin|last2=Nolan|first3=Rocco|last3=Parascandola|first4=Larry|last4=McShane|work=[[Daily News (New York)|New York Daily News]]|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=April 8, 2015}}</ref>
